note: Human-reviewed identity mappings. Each entry is a decision a machine may not make: it binds a catalog model id to an exact upstream benchmark id. Every entry needs a reason a later reader can re-verify from primary sources. An entry whose target leaves the upstream index resolves to nothing rather than to a guess.

evidence: context_length: Ollama reports 262144; the chosen target reports 262144, the rejected one 256000 — an exact match on one side and a mismatch on the other
general.architecture: Ollama reports 'nemotron-3-nano'; the rejected candidate is 'nemotron-3-nano-omni', a different architecture
modality: Ollama reports capabilities [completion, tools, thinking] with no vision or audio, and the chosen target is text-only; the rejected candidate accepts text, audio, image and video
tags: https://ollama.com/library/nemotron-3-nano/tags lists 30b, 30b-a3b-fp16, 30b-a3b-q4, 30b-a3b-q8, 30b-cloud — no omni build is published at all
nemotron-3-nano:30b.reverifyBy: re-running the /api/show call above and comparing context_length and architecture; if either stops matching, delete this mapping rather than adjusting it

evidence: general.parameter_count: Ollama reports 550000000000, and the target's own id declares 550b — an exact match on the one number that identifies this model
NVIDIA publishes exactly one Nemotron 3 Ultra, so there is no sibling for the parameter count to be confused with
context differs (Ollama 262144 vs the target's 512288), which is expected: a host may serve a shorter window than the model supports. The parameter count, not the served window, is the identity
nemotron-3-ultra.reverifyBy: if NVIDIA ever ships a second Ultra at a different parameter count, this mapping must be re-decided rather than kept

evidence: general.parameter_count: Ollama reports 120000000000; the target declares 120b
general.architecture: Ollama reports 'nemotron_h_moe', a mixture-of-experts model, consistent with the target's 'a12b' active-parameter suffix

nemotron-3-ultra-free.decidedBy: models.dev provider 'opencode', plus the reference index's own free variant
evidence: context: models.dev reports 1000000 for opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free, which is exactly the context the reference index publishes for nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free (the paid variant reports 512288)
OpenCode Zen sells no paid nemotron-3-ultra, so the -free suffix is the plan and not a distinct model
the reference index publishes identical benchmark values for the paid and :free variants, so binding to the base is the same claim either way

rejected.note: Mappings that looked reasonable and were REFUSED on evidence. Recorded so the same plausible-but-wrong bind is not proposed again.

qwen3.5-plus.why: context mismatch of roughly 4x: models.dev reports 262144 for both opencode/qwen3.5-plus and opencode-go/qwen3.5-plus, while the dated snapshot reports 1000000. A dated snapshot may well be the same family, but nothing available establishes it is the same model, and a wrong bind would attach another model's benchmark.

mimo-v2-pro.why: OpenCode Go sells mimo-v2-pro AND mimo-v2.5-pro as two separate models in the same roster. The provider itself distinguishes them, so binding one to the other would merge two products a seller lists apart. The matching context window (1048576 for both) is what makes this bind tempting and is not identity evidence.

mimo-v2-omni.why: same as mimo-v2-pro: a version change (v2 vs v2.5) that the provider's own roster keeps distinct.

mistral-large-3:675b.why: no 675b Mistral Large exists in the reference index. Binding to mistral-large-2512 would be a size and edition collapse.

deepseek-v4-flash:preview.why: a preview build with no counterpart published anywhere. Binding it to the stable deepseek-v4-flash would claim a preview and a release are the same model.
